source_read: Independently read the frozen brief, task and claim context and the original supplied Lynskey2003 PDF (printed pp.427-433). Made and visually inspected own 300-dpi renders of pp.428,429,431,432 in /workspace/scratch/d1ee8d93ce58/tmp/pdfs/reader420. No other reader outputs, cards, adjudication logs, external sources or underlying cited studies read. No calculations were needed for this diagnostic/temporal/covariate qualification.

results.note: The substantive qualification is supported, with attribution and locator refinements. The at-least-monthly gate begins at the bottom of p.428, not p.429. Page 429 explicitly describes two abuse symptoms, four dependence symptoms and the thresholds stated in the task; its explicit statement about not providing formal DSM-IV criteria applies to the dependence measure. Calling the overall drug-problem criteria modified is supported by the described operationalization, but should not be presented as a direct author statement that both measures lack formal criteria. Full DSM-IV lifetime alcohol dependence is explicit on p.429. The lack of ages at progression or problem onset is explicit in the second Comment paragraph on p.431, which continues on p.432. The consequence for temporal ordering is an editorial inference from that limitation and the lifetime outcomes; it is not a directly reported analysis of problem-onset order. This should be distinguished from the paper's separate treatment of order of drug initiation on p.430. The described covariates support the limited negative statement that peer affiliation and temperament are not described as measured/adjusted covariates in this paper; they do not establish their nonmeasurement in the broader register or survey. Separate MZ/DZ analyses are explicitly reported under Subsidiary Analyses on p.431, specifically with early-use cutoffs before 15, 16 and 18 years; their numerical estimates are not printed. The task locator omitted this section, and its extraction should identify the alternate cutoffs rather than imply printed separate estimates for the principal before-17 comparison.
results.corrected_extracted: For cannabis, sedatives, cocaine/other stimulants and opioids, respondents reporting at least monthly use were asked additional drug-problem questions (pp.428-429). Abuse was operationalized as either of two symptoms, and dependence as at least two of four symptoms. The authors explicitly say the dependence measure did not provide formal DSM-IV criteria; the described drug-problem operationalization uses modified criteria. Lifetime alcohol dependence, in contrast, was assessed using full DSM-IV criteria (p.429). The authors explicitly acknowledge lacking ages at progression to more frequent use or onset of problems (p.431, Comment, second paragraph continuing p.432). Consequently, the lifetime drug-problem/alcohol-dependence comparisons do not by themselves establish the timing of problem onset relative to early cannabis initiation (editorial inference); order of drug initiation was separately considered. The paper's described control variables include conduct disorder, major depression, a nondiagnostic social-anxiety measure, early tobacco use and early regular alcohol use. Peer affiliation and temperament are not described as measured covariates in this paper (editorial reading of this report, not evidence that the broader register never measured them). Under Subsidiary Analyses, the authors report separate monozygotic and dizygotic analyses using early-use cutoffs before ages 15, 16 and 18, stating that they confirmed the previous conclusions; no numerical estimates for these separate analyses are printed (p.431).
